## How they got there
Real Madrid secured the title by beating Borussia Dortmund 2-0 in the final. Their profile during the group and league phases was defined by exceptional efficiency, as they recorded 3.0 points per game to beat 98% of teams, while also generating 61.0 attacks per game to outperform 91% of their peers. Additionally, they maintained a goal difference of 1.5 per game, which placed them ahead of 91% of the season's group and league-phase participants.

## Would the model have picked them?
The model would have selected Real Madrid, ranking them second inside its top two predictions for this tournament. With a calculated probability of 32.0% to reach the final, the system viewed their chances as significantly higher than the base rate of 12.5% for a random knockout team. Consequently, the statistical expectation aligned with reaching the quarter-finals, which is the stage nearest to the model's projected value of 1.36 on its scale.

## Weak spots
The analysis identifies two clear areas where the team beat fewer than half of the teams in the league or group phase: long passes at 7.9% and distance covered per game at 113.1 km. These statistics represent the lowest points in their performance profile, with the club beating only 3% of peers on passing volume and just 9% on total distance. While other metrics like shot accuracy showed a lower standing relative to historical data, these two specific figures constitute the distinct weak spots for this squad.

messages.content: You are a football performance analyst writing for a curious, data-literate reader. Use ONLY the facts provided. Quote every number exactly as it appears in the facts, with the same rounding. Do not introduce players, managers, matches, events, analyses or numbers that are not in the facts. 'Better than this %' figures say how many teams the club beat on a stat, so higher is always better, including for stats marked '(lower is better)', where beating a team means having the lower value. Write them as 'better than X% of teams', never as 'top X%'. SHAP contributions are measured in knockout stages: a positive contribution means the stat pushed the model's expected stage up by that fraction of a round, a negative one pushed it down. A SHAP contribution is the model's view, not a measure of how good the team was at the stat: a team can rank high on a stat the model marked down, so never call a stat a strength or a weakness because of its SHAP sign. Everything here is a statistical association, not a cause: never say a stat or a team's profile drove, powered, propelled, carried, helped, hindered or prevented a result, and do not explain why a stat got its contribution. Write plain markdown without tables.
